title: LFG: Looking for Group
text: LFG means Looking for Group: a player seeks a party.
usage: Interpret it as a recruitment term in game chat. It does not prove that a group already exists.

sources.title: Wowhead: Classic WoW Glossary and Common Terms Explained

title: LFM: Looking for More
text: LFM means Looking for More. LF1M and LF2M request one or two more players.
usage: Use nearby role and dungeon names to understand the vacancy. Do not infer a complete party composition.

sources.title: Wowhead: Classic WoW Glossary and Common Terms Explained

title: DPS: damage rate or damage role
text: DPS means damage per second. In recruitment, it can mean a damage dealer.
usage: Distinguish a measured value from a party slot. Do not infer a player damage value from item level.

sources.title: Wowhead: Classic WoW Glossary and Common Terms Explained

title: OT: off-tank
text: In English raid role chat, OT usually means the secondary tank.
usage: Chinese combat chat often uses OT for lost threat control. Resolve the community and context before choosing a meaning.

sources.title: Wowhead: Classic WoW Glossary and Common Terms Explained

title: Aggro: enemy attention
text: Aggro refers to hostile attention. Threat describes the system behind much enemy target selection.
usage: Special mechanics can override normal target selection. Do not infer exact threat thresholds from this term.

sources.title: Wowhead: Classic WoW Glossary and Common Terms Explained

title: Adds: additional enemies
text: Adds are additional enemies involved in an encounter.
usage: Some adds come from intended mechanics. Others join after an accidental pull. Do not assign blame from the word alone.

sources.title: Wowhead: Classic WoW Glossary and Common Terms Explained

title: Wipe: group defeat
text: A wipe is an attempt in which the group is defeated or cannot continue.
usage: Acknowledge frustration before joking. Revival rules differ in Hardcore modes.

sources.title: Wowhead: Classic WoW Glossary and Common Terms Explained

title: SM: Scarlet Monastery
text: In English dungeon recruitment, SM commonly refers to Scarlet Monastery.
usage: The same letters often mean Shaman in Chinese class chat. Confirm the dungeon version before discussing its layout or bosses.

title: You are not prepared
text: A well-known Illidan line, reused by players as a preparation joke.
usage: Use sparingly when the user invites banter or discusses Illidan. Original companion example: “Then let us check repairs before the dramatic entrance.”

title: Zug zug
text: Zug zug is an Orcish acknowledgement associated with Warcraft orc units. Players reuse it as playful agreement.
usage: Use it for brief, friendly banter when the user welcomes Warcraft humour. It does not imply an instruction to attack or a particular faction identity.
